findings.issue: The acceptance gate is incomplete: Read/ReadTo/ExtractTo now call Checks.EnsureAcceptable(), but SetupPackage.Content is still a plain public property handed out on a refused file. Examine() builds the SetupPackage with the parsed setup.json whatever the verdict (line 487), and SetupContent carries DeviceSeed (the device's Ed25519+X25519 private seeds) and OfficeKey. So on a file refused for OtherDevice/Older/Revoked/Employee/Organisation, `inspection.Package!.Content.DeviceSeed` and `.OfficeKey` are the decrypted payload of a refused setup file, reachable without any gate — exactly the exposure finding 1 named, and the review's own security criterion 'no payload of a refused setup file can be read' is therefore not met. It is worse than no gate, because Read(SetupEntryNames.Content) now throws while the adjacent property returns the same secrets parsed, so a B1 caller will reasonably believe the object is safe.
findings.fix: Split the description from the secrets. Keep a new always-readable projection for the screen — e.g. `public SetupDescription Description` carrying FormatVersion, ExportedAt, ExportSeq, Org (id/name/cycleStartDay/numberingFormat/public keys), Units, Office, Device (id/deviceNo/role/syncScope/certificate), Employee and Includes, i.e. everything W03 renders next to the check list — and turn `Content` into `public SetupContent Content { get { Checks.EnsureAcceptable(); return _content; } }` (the checker already holds the record internally, so nothing inside the library changes). Add a test beside No_entry_may_be_read_out_of_a_file_whose_checks_did_not_all_pass asserting that `package.Content` throws on the same OtherDevice package while `package.Description.Org.Name` still works.

findings.issue: SetupExpectations.FirstRun (line 34) is now a landmine: it has no StagingDirectory, so every Inspect/Open call made with it throws CryptoException(ErrorCode.Corrupt) — and its XML doc still reads 'A machine that has never been activated: nothing is pinned yet', i.e. it still advertises itself as the first-run value W02 should pass. The test suite works around this with a private WithStaging() helper, so no test exercises the API the way a host would write it. Worse, Corrupt is the code B1 will map to the Arabic 'the file is damaged' message, so a host configuration mistake is reported to the user as a damaged setup file.
findings.fix: Remove the parameterless FirstRun property and replace it with `public static SetupExpectations FirstRun(string stagingDirectory) => new() { StagingDirectory = stagingDirectory };` (the writer's internal Verify call, which never goes through Validate, can use `new SetupExpectations { StagingDirectory = "x" }` or a dedicated internal instance). If the property must stay for source compatibility, update its XML doc to say the caller must still set StagingDirectory, and give the missing-staging refusal its own message distinct from file damage so B1 does not map it to the damaged-file text.

findings.issue: ReadLogoPreviewFromRejectedFile (line 178) is the one deliberate gate bypass, and it is unbounded and undeclared-entry-tolerant. It calls DecryptEntry -> ContainerReader.ReadEntry, whose only size bound is CopyWithLimit(expected.Size) — the size the manifest declares. On a first run nothing is pinned, so a hostile file signed with its own root key and opened with its own package password can declare logo.png at any size and this method materialises the whole thing as a managed byte[]. It also ignores Content.Includes.Logo, so it will return an entry the Logo check has already refused as Tampered. This is the same threat model the new manifest bound and the Argon2 ceiling were added for.
findings.fix: In ReadLogoPreviewFromRejectedFile, look the entry up in _reader.Manifest.Entries first and throw CryptoException(ErrorCode.Corrupt) when entry.Size exceeds a stated maximum (A04 caps the uploaded logo at 2 MB, so `public const int MaxLogoSize = 2 * 1024 * 1024`), and return null unless Content.Includes.Logo is true so a logo the description never declared is never previewed. Add two tests: a package whose manifest declares an oversized logo.png is refused by the preview, and a package carrying logo.png with includes.logo=false previews nothing.

findings.issue: Finding 7 normalised ErrorCode.Expired to Package/FutureDate on the root-certificate path, but CheckDevice (line 249) still returns the raw chain error, and CertificateChain.VerifyNode raises Expired for a device certificate whose IssuedAt sits more than CertificateChain.ClockSkew ahead of the clock. So a file whose exportedAt is fine but whose device certificate is dated ahead still lands as SetupCheckItem.Device / ErrorCode.Expired — a code W03's vocabulary has no Arabic word for, which is precisely the inconsistency finding 7 set out to remove.
findings.fix: In SetupChecker.CheckDevice, after `if (!CertificateChain.TryVerify(...))`, translate the date case the same way Examine now does: `return error == ErrorCode.Expired ? ErrorCode.FutureDate : error;` (Revoked, BadSignature and Tampered keep passing through unchanged). Add a test that builds a device certificate issued two days ahead of the clock while exportedAt stays at now, and asserts SetupCheckItem.Device carries ErrorCode.FutureDate.

findings.issue: The cache threshold boundary disagrees three ways. The XML doc on MaxCachedEntrySize (line 81) says 'At or above it ... the entry is decrypted again on every call', the test is named Small_entries_stay_cached_but_one_at_the_cache_threshold_or_larger_is_decrypted_again_each_time, but ExceedsCacheThreshold (line 139) uses `entry.Size > MaxCachedEntrySize`, so an entry of exactly 1 MB IS cached — and the test only ever exercises MaxCachedEntrySize + 1, so the 'at the threshold' half of its own name is neither true nor covered.
findings.fix: Pick one: either change line 139 to `entry.Size >= MaxCachedEntrySize` (matching the doc and the test name, and add a case with an entry of exactly MaxCachedEntrySize asserting Assert.NotSame), or reword the XML doc to 'Larger than this' and rename the test to ..._but_one_larger_than_the_cache_threshold_is_decrypted_again_each_time.

findings.issue: ReadEntryTo (line 232) writes every decrypted byte into the caller's destination and only then calls CheckEntry, so on a size/hash mismatch the caller is left holding partial content that was never confirmed against the manifest, and the XML doc says only 'checking its recorded size and hash on the way'. ExtractTo has the same shape and additionally leaves the partial file on disk in the installation folder when CheckEntry throws. Neither behaviour is documented, and SetupPackage.ReadTo inherits it silently.
findings.fix: Say it explicitly in the XML docs of ContainerReader.ReadEntryTo and SetupPackage.ReadTo: on CryptoException the destination has already received unverified bytes and the caller must discard it. For ExtractTo, wrap the per-entry write in try/catch and delete the partial target file before rethrowing, so a refused container never leaves a half-written file behind on a first run. Add a test that a tampered entry leaves no file at the extraction target.

missing_spec_items: Package validity window (not part of this package's nine-item spec — supervisor decision needed). The approved W03 reference screens (design/exports/light|dark/W/W03 — التشغيل الأول — فحص الحزمة والتفعيل.png) render a first-class refusal dialog «تعذّر قبول حزمة التفعيل / انتهت صلاحية الحزمة في 05/09/2026 — مدة صلاحية الحزمة انقضت قبل 7 أيام ولم تعد مقبولة للتفعيل», and docs/design/SCREENS.md row W03 lists «حالة خطأ: حزمة غير صالحة/منتهية». Nothing in the reader can produce that state: SetupExpectations has no maximum package age, SetupChecker.CheckPackage checks only FormatVersion, ExportSeq, entry names, FutureDate and Older, and CertificateChain's maxAge parameter is never passed by the setup path. B1's W03 will have no code to bind that dialog to. Either add SetupExpectations.MaxPackageAge with CheckPackage returning ErrorCode.Expired on SetupCheckItem.Package (and record the rule in ARCHITECTURE §4, whose refusal list omits it), or strike the expiry state from W03 and SCREENS.md.

Check-list arity and the advisory status (interface-side, for B1's notes, not a defect in this package). W03 shows exactly seven lines and the footer «اكتمل الفحص — 7 من 7 عناصر، تنبيه واحد لا يمنع التفعيل», while SetupCheckItem now emits up to twelve (Package, Signature, Organisation, Office, Device, Employee, OfficeKey, Logo, Guide, ReportTemplate, LetterTemplate, Revocation). The screen's non-blocking «تنبيه» (the logo-resolution advisory) also has no counterpart in SetupCheckStatus, which is Ok/Failed/Absent and where any Failed — including an optional item — makes IsAcceptable false. B1 must own both the projection to seven rows and the advisory state.
notes:
COMMANDS. Ran exactly `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Crypto` then `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests` from D:\AI\Administration2. Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. Tests: Failed 0, Passed 224, Skipped 0, Total 224, 15 s — the 212 baseline plus the 12 new facts, nothing regressed. I modified no file and ran no git command beyond read-only status/diff. The package touches no WPF host and no Blazor page, so the host-launch rule does not apply; I did view the W03 light and dark reference PNGs, which is where the one screen-level gap above came from.

SPEC ITEM BY ITEM — all nine are implemented.
(1) SetupPackage.Read, ReadTo and ExtractTo call Checks.EnsureAcceptable() as the first statement after the disposal check, and TryRead/ReadLogo/ReadGuide/ReadReportTemplate/ReadLetterTemplate inherit it through Read. No_entry_may_be_read_out_of_a_file_whose_checks_did_not_all_pass pins all four entry points against a genuine OtherDevice refusal (container, signature and password all held, so a SetupPackage really does exist), which is the right shape for the test. The named exception ReadLogoPreviewFromRejectedFile is a defensible judgement: SCREENS.md W03 asks for «بطاقة معلومات بالمؤسسة والشعار» alongside the error states, the logo carries no secret, and by the time the object exists the signature and the package password have held. The XML doc states the reasoning. The residual hole is Content, reported as the medium finding above.
(2) StagingDirectory is enforced in SetupPackageReader.Validate (reached from both Inspect overloads, and therefore from both Open overloads) and in SetupPackageWriter.Prepare (reached from both Write overloads), both with CryptoException(Corrupt), both with XML docs naming the host's own protected folder and saying why. ContainerOpenOptions/ContainerWriteRequest keep StagingDirectory optional for the other container kinds, which matches the finding's scope. The cleartext-in-%TEMP% path is genuinely closed for setup files: ContainerReader.DecryptPayload and ContainerWriter.Write both take the value straight from the request, and ContainerWriter.CreateStagingFile only falls back to Path.GetTempPath() when it is empty, which the setup layer can no longer be.
(5) The chosen shape is the second of the two the finding offered — `internal Argon2Params? Kdf` plus `request.Kdf ?? Argon2Params.CreateDefault()` in BuildRequest — rather than an upward clamp. I checked that this is airtight and not merely nominal: Wakeel.Crypto.csproj grants InternalsVisibleTo to Wakeel.Crypto.Tests and nothing else, so no production assembly can set the property at all and every setup file built outside this project gets 64 MB / 3 / 2. The_writer_uses_the_products_full_argon2_cost_when_no_internal_test_hook_is_supplied asserts the three values on the written manifest and is not a tautology (it pays the real Argon2 cost once).
(6) ContainerReader.ReadEntryTo mirrors ExtractTo's streaming shape exactly (HashingStream over the destination, CopyWithLimit against the declared size, CheckEntry afterwards) and SetupPackage.ReadTo forwards to it behind the same gate. The cache threshold is a public documented const and the Assert.Same / Assert.NotSame pair in Small_entries_stay_cached... is real behavioural evidence, not a restatement. Boundary wording is the low finding above.
(7) Correct, and I verified the code comment's load-bearing claim rather than taking it: in Examine, TryVerify is called with revocations: null and the default maxAge: null, so of CertificateChain's four Expired sites (lines 55, 60, 185, 190) only line 185 — the certificate's own IssuedAt ahead of now + ClockSkew — is reachable, exactly as the comment says. A_root_certificate_dated_ahead_of_the_clock_is_a_future_dated_package_not_a_bad_signature reaches it the only honest way, through a test helper that dates the root independently of the container clock and of exportedAt. One nuance for B1: the root-date tolerance is CertificateChain.ClockSkew (1 day), not expectations.MaxFutureSkew, so a host that widens MaxFutureSkew past a day gets the container check passing and the chain check failing — both report Package/FutureDate, so the screen stays coherent, but the two tolerances are not the same number.
(8) ReadAll(entry, limit) enforces 1 MB while the bytes are still being inflated, for manifest.json and signature.bin alike, and throws Corrupt. Both new ContainerTests are real (a 2 MB padded field and a 2 MB signature, each of which compresses to almost nothing, so they are decompression bombs in miniature). One caveat on what they prove: since ReadAll would refuse an over-limit entry either way, these two cases do not actually distinguish 'bounded during decompression' from 'bounded after buffering' — the code is right, the tests are just weaker than their comment claims. If you want the property pinned, assert it with an entry whose inflated size is orders of magnitude past the bound.
(9) Matches ARCHITECTURE §4 line 82 exactly, which already names includes.letterTemplate and letter-template.docx: SetupIncludes gained a fourth field, SetupEntryNames.LetterTemplate is "letter-template.docx", SetupCheckItem.LetterTemplate sits beside ReportTemplate, SetupChecker's allowlist and Optional() cover it, the writer has a LetterTemplate factory, and SetupPackage.ReadLetterTemplate() reads it. Round trips both with and without it are asserted, the canonical-JSON field-name test pins "letterTemplate", and A_letter_template_entry_the_description_never_declared_is_refused pins the declared/present symmetry.

PUBLIC API CHANGES FOR THE B1 BUILDERS (all minimal, none with an existing consumer — I grepped src and tests outside Wakeel.Crypto and found no reference to any Setup type). Breaking: SetupIncludes gains a fourth positional parameter (arity 3 -> 4); SetupWriteRequest.Kdf becomes internal; SetupExpectations.StagingDirectory and SetupWriteRequest.StagingDirectory become effectively required; SetupCheckItem.LetterTemplate is inserted before Revocation, which shifts Revocation's ordinal from 10 to 11 — harmless today because the enum is a display order and is never persisted, but B1 must not store it as a number. Added: SetupPackage.ReadTo(string, Stream), SetupPackage.MaxCachedEntrySize, SetupPackage.ReadLetterTemplate(), SetupPackage.ReadLogoPreviewFromRejectedFile(), ContainerReader.ReadEntryTo(string, ContainerKeySource, Stream), SetupEntryNames.LetterTemplate, SetupCheckItem.LetterTemplate.

HYGIENE. Only src/Wakeel.Crypto/{Containers/ContainerReader.cs, Setup/SetupChecker.cs, Setup/SetupChecks.cs, Setup/SetupContent.cs, Setup/SetupPackageReader.cs, Setup/SetupPackageWriter.cs} and tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests/{ContainerTests.cs, SetupPackageTests.cs} are dirty for this package. Wakeel.Crypto.csproj is untouched and still references only the two centrally pinned packages — no NuGet package was added. Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Wakeel.slnx and docs/ are clean. The other dirty paths (Wakeel.Core/Services/OfficialNumberService.cs, Wakeel.Design, Wakeel.UI, their tests) belong to the concurrent packages, not this one.

LANGUAGE AND RTL. Not applicable in the usual sense and correctly so: I grepped src/Wakeel.Crypto for Arabic script and found zero characters in zero files. Every new message is an English developer string on a CryptoException, and the Arabic is owned entirely by the interface layer through the SetupCheckItem / ErrorCode vocabulary. No icon-only buttons, no bidi surface in this package.

WHY 'fix' RATHER THAN 'accept'. Build and tests are green, all nine items are implemented and each is pinned by a test that would fail if the code were reverted, and five of the six findings are low. The blocker is the single medium: the stated security criterion for this package is that no payload of a refused setup file can be read, and SetupPackage.Content still hands the device seeds and the office key out of exactly such a file. It is a contained fix — a redacted Description projection plus a gated Content getter plus one test — after which I would accept.
